mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a robust economy, leading to higher consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during early-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05), or GDP growth rate does not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during late-cycle contractions (t-test p > 0.05), or unemployment rate does not lead to decreased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a strong supply chain, leading to increased economic growth and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when industrial production is increasing (t-test p > 0.05), or industrial production does not lead to increased economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts increase and GDP growth rate is strong, it signals a robust economy, leading to higher consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in early-cycle expansions are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low and inflation is high, it signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during monetary easing cycles (t-test p > 0.05), or federal funds rate and inflation do not lead to increased borrowing and spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is increasing, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during late-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05), or unemployment rate and payroll employment do not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production is increasing and housing starts are strong, it signals a robust supply chain, leading to increased economic growth and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in early-cycle expansions are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
